Author: Techdamentals
Text: $XOM An integrated company pumps crude and refines it, which means it sits on both sides of what the inflation report is measuring. Crude is the raw material. The CPI tracks the finished products: gasoline at 2.9% of the basket, plus fuel oil, electricity and natural gas. In the twelve months to August those finished products rose far faster than the barrel they came from, and that gap is a refining story rather than an oil story. Full explainer, plain English: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=le-mFDuzQd8 Written version: https://techdamentals.com/newsletter/why-cpi-and-core-inflation-tell-different-stories?ref=st Educational, not advice.

Author: Techdamentals
Text: $XOM is one of the largest producers of the crude oil that becomes the gasoline and distillate fuels driving the gap between headline and core inflation this year. Headline CPI counts energy prices directly; core inflation strips them out because food and energy swing on weather and oil markets rather than broad demand. In August, energy was up 16.3% while core ran at 2.4%. Exxon's business spans both the crude that feeds refineries and the refining that turns it into fuel, so its results touch the same barrel behind gasoline's 27.4% yearly gain.
